name: Laser Ranging Retroreflector
greeting: I am… a mirror panel left by Apollo 11. I still work today!

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: Apollo 11 astronauts set up this panel of special mirrors on the Moon in July 1969.

script.speaker: equipment
script.text: Shine a laser at me from Earth, and I'll bounce the light straight back to where it came from.

script.speaker: scientist
script.text: So we can time the light and work out how far away the Moon is?

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: These measurements show the Moon is slowly drifting away from Earth, by roughly 3.8 cm every year.

moreInfo.text: A retroreflector uses corner-cube prisms that always send light back in the direction it came from. Observatories on Earth still fire lasers at the Apollo reflectors and time the round trip to measure the Earth–Moon distance.

questions.question: What have measurements using this equipment shown?
options: The Moon is moving closer to Earth
The Moon is drifting away from Earth by about 3.8 cm a year
questions.explanation: Timing laser pulses bounced off the reflectors shows the Moon slowly moving away from us.
